About the tune

  • Music (1898): Josiah Booth (1852–1929)

Metre: 7.3.7.3.7.7.7.3.

Melody from the Christian Classics Ethereal Hymnary (CCEH, public domain); tune LIMPSFIELD by Josiah Booth (1852–1929). The CCEH gives its tunes as four-part scores; this page has the melody only, read from its MIDI file and checked against its incipit, and NoteFusion's engine wrote the solfa from the notes. It has not yet been checked against a printed hymn book.

Questions about Limpsfield

What is the doh of Limpsfield?

In this version, in D major, doh is D. If your choir sings it in another key, doh moves to the new key note and every solfa syllable stays the same — that is what movable doh means.

What note does Limpsfield start on?

It starts on s (A in D major). Find doh first, then sing up or down to s.

What words can be sung to Limpsfield?

Limpsfield is in the metre 7.3.7.3.7.7.7.3: lines of 7, 3, 7, 3, 7, 7, 7, 3 syllables. Words written in the same metre fit it; check where the stresses fall before you sing them together.

Is Limpsfield in the public domain?

Yes. Josiah Booth died in 1929; the tune was first published in 1898. Everyone named died before 1955 and it was published before 1929, so the tune is out of copyright in Nigeria, the UK, the EU and the United States. Modern arrangements of it can still be under copyright.
